evidence_summary: Municipal SAAE reports 622 L/s treated production, about 435 L/s reaching roughly 87,000 registered residences and about 187 L/s lost in distribution; restructuring and investment are underway.

Second stage of Adutora da Fé received an order of service with approximately R$230 million of investment; the project expands São Francisco-derived water infrastructure toward Bom Jesus da Lapa and surrounding municipalities.
Municipality announced water rationing and temporary suspension in the municipal seat during the dry season because of reduced availability.
Municipality reported progression of a planned approximately 70 km adductor with pumping stations, distribution, storage and a new treatment plant; project-design procurement had been completed.
Municipality reported procurement advancing for the second stage of Barragem de Cristalândia, expected to increase storage capacity by about 40 percent and reinforce regional water security.
Icó is included among municipalities receiving new rural-community water-supply systems under Projeto São José IV. This is evidence of public investment but not industrial or urban spare capacity.
Water-system improvements increased production at ETA ZPE from about 70,000 to 100,000 L/h; the regional treatment/distribution system is being modernized.
A third distribution pump at ETA 01 was reported to raise distribution capacity for targeted neighborhoods from roughly 550,000 to 720,000 L/h.
